title: Embeddability between 3-manifolds is not stable
summary: We prove that given two compact oriented $3$-manifolds $N$ and $M,$ with $M$ satisfying only a mild hypothesis, there is a hyperbolic $3$-manifold $N'$ arbitrarily ``closely related'' to $N,$ and such that $N'$ does not embed in $M.$ For instance, as a weak version of our main theorem, if $M$ is a rational homology sphere then for any $k\geq 1$ the $3$-manifold $N'$ can be chosen to be $Y_k$-equivalent to $N.$ Our techniques rely on the construction of $3$-manifolds with complicated Frohman--Kania-Bartoszyńska ideals, using the strong approximation for…
